latest_findings.claim: At e<=0.6 (N=64, seeds 70-72, 10-step checkpoints), the layer-4 accel_step best-of-5 control R2 is 0.667-0.682 in all 3 seeds, inside the predicted [0.58, 0.70] band. The other two predictions were met in only some seeds. Final accel_step margin is 0.187 (seed 71), 0.191 (seed 70) and 0.204 (seed 72), so only seed 72 reaches the 0.20 bar, though no seed falls to the <=0.18 'false' bar. Raw R2 is 0.868-0.871 in all 3 seeds. The persistent 0.1-bar formation step read from the trajectories is 80 (seed 71, margin 0.113), 70 or 80 (seed 70: exactly 0.100 at step 70, while formed_at_step says 80) and 60 (seed 72). Force is much weaker than accel_step: R2 0.46-0.58 at layer 4 with margins of 0.075 (fails), 0.105 and 0.140.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Only the control R2 prediction held in all 3 seeds. The margin prediction (>=0.20) holds in 1 of 3 seeds. The timing prediction (<=75) holds in 1 seed, fails in seed 71 (step 80), and is undecidable in seed 70, where the margin is exactly 0.100 at step 70 and formed_at_step reports 80. So neither the 'all 3 seeds' true condition nor the '2 of 3 seeds' false condition is cleanly met. The e<=0.6 values lie between the e<=0.5 and e<=0.7 regimes as quoted in the open questions (margin about 0.13-0.17 / 0.19 / 0.24-0.26; formation about 65-100 / 60-80 / 60-70). That fits a gradual shift better than a switch at or below 0.6, but it is not a clean refutation. The control R2 fell only about 0.06 from e<=0.5 to e<=0.6 but about 0.12 from 0.6 to 0.7, which points to a non-linear control decline. Raw accel_step R2 (about 0.87) looks close to the e<=0.5 values, so most of the margin gain may come from the falling control rather than better decoding. Headroom-normalized margins are 0.59-0.61. Caveats: the e<=0.5 and e<=0.7 comparison numbers come from other experiments with different seeds, some with 5-step checkpoints, while this run uses 10-step spacing, so a difference of one checkpoint (10 steps) decides the timing criterion. What would change the verdict: rerunning e<=0.5, 0.6 and 0.7 on the same seeds 70-72 with 5-step checkpoints, plus a documented rule for whether a margin exactly at 0.100 counts as crossing the bar. Other observations: val_mse_ratio at formation is 2.9-3.5, between the reported e<=0.5 band (2.1-3.3) and the e<=0.7 band (2.9-4.1). Distance forms at steps 30-40, 20-50 steps before accel_step. The early force transient appears again (margin 0.08-0.125 at steps 10-20, falling to 0.001-0.033 by steps 40-50).

latest_findings.claim: The paired delay this experiment was designed to test could not be computed. The N=64 per-seed trajectories for seeds 56, 57, 58, 62 and 63 were not in the provided results, and the lab files could not be opened. All 5 N=256 runs completed and meet the side conditions: final accel_step margin is 0.118 to 0.187 at layer 4 (R2 0.85 to 0.90, controls 0.67 to 0.78, so >= 0.1 in every seed), and val_mse_ratio ends at 11.3 to 13.3 (above 1). From the 5-step trajectories, the half-final step (seeds 56/57/58/62/63) is 85/75/100/90/95, a range of 25 steps, and the persistent 0.1-bar step is 95/155/115/95/100, a range of 60 steps. Only two N=64 values can be paired, both quoted in an open question: seed 56 at step 80 and seed 62 at step 100. That gives 0.1-bar delays of +15 and -5. Force has no lasting signal: an early transient margin of 0.16 to 0.21 at steps 10-15 falls to about 0 to 0.02 by steps 105-120, compared with accel_step's 0.12 to 0.19.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The primary criterion, a half-final delay of at least +15 in 4 of 5 seeds with a mean of at least +20, needs the per-seed N=64 half-final steps, and they were not available to this analysis. The verdict is inconclusive because data was missing, not because the effect is absent. Joining the N=64 arm trajectories from the 5-step N=64 runs of these seeds and recomputing the delays would decide supported or refuted. Three caveats from the N=256 arm itself. (1) The two pairable 0.1-bar delays (+15, -5) are smaller than the earlier 10-step comparison for seeds 56-58 (+20/+70/+30), so some of the earlier delay may have come from mixed checkpoint spacing. (2) The half-final measure is tighter than the 0.1 bar within N=256 (25 vs 60 steps), but it is confounded with plateau height. Seed 57 has the lowest final margin (0.118, control 0.778) and so the earliest half-final step (75), yet the latest 0.1-bar step (155). It dwells at 0.093-0.099 from step 125 to 150. (3) For seed 62, probes_final.formed_at_step = 100, but the trajectory first crosses persistently at 95, another case of the one-checkpoint lag. All 5 runs completed 300/300 steps with 5 controls each.

latest_findings.claim: At 5-step checkpoint spacing, seeds 56, 57, 58, 62 and 63 (N=64, e<=0.5) first hold the accel_step margin at or above 0.1 for good at steps 80, 85, 90, 100 and 95. That is the same 80-100 window seen at 10-step spacing, so checkpoint resolution does not explain it. Half-final steps, read from the trajectories, are 70, 65, 70, 60 and 85, and only 3 of 5 seeds (56, 57, 58) meet both expected-if-true ranges. Final accel_step R2 is 0.875-0.909 against controls of 0.709-0.769 (margins 0.139-0.173). Force never beats its control: final margins are 0.051-0.080, after an early transient of 0.15-0.17 at steps 10-15 that falls to about 0 by step 40.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Neither preset outcome happened. Expected-if-true needed 4 of 5 seeds in range on both measures, but only 3 of 5 qualified: seed 62's persistent step is 100 and seed 63's half-final step is 85. Expected-if-false needed 3 of 5 seeds out of range, but only those same 2 were. The other conditions held: all 5 runs completed 300/300 steps, every final margin is at least 0.1, and val_mse_ratio is 0.66-0.70 at step 200, first dropping below 1 at steps 140-160. The data do go against the stated hypothesis. Persistent formation at 80-100 matches the earlier 10-step reads for these seeds (56-58 were 80/90/90 at 10-step spacing). Seeds 65-69 (65-90) sit only about 10-15 steps earlier, which is inside the seed-to-seed spread. So the earlier window looks like ordinary seed variation, not a resolution artifact. The 0.1-bar step is fragile when a run levels off near the threshold: seed 62 stays at a margin of 0.095-0.097 from step 80 to 95 and crosses only at 100. The two timing measures also order seeds differently (seed 62 has the earliest half-final step and the latest persistent step). In all 5 runs formed_at_step equals the trajectory crossing, with no one-checkpoint lag. Per-seed control R2 does not order the persistent steps (seed 57 has the highest control, 0.769, but forms at 85). What would change the verdict: a pre-registered single criterion, or more 5-step seeds, showing the 65-90 and 80-100 groups differ by more than their within-group spread.

latest_findings.claim: At e in [0, 0.7] (N=64, 4 layers, d_model=64, m2 in [0.1, 1]), the layer-4 accel_step best-of-5 control R2 was 0.543, 0.553 and 0.559 (seeds 72, 70, 71). That sits between the e <= 0.5 controls (0.71-0.77) and the e <= 0.85 controls (0.25-0.35). The final accel_step margins were 0.257, 0.260 and 0.241 (R2 0.80-0.81), and accel_step first stayed above the 0.1 margin at steps 60, 60 and 70. Force was much weaker: margins 0.140 (layer 4), 0.101 (layer 3) and 0.121 (layer 1), against controls of 0.27-0.39. Measured against available headroom, accel_step reached about 0.55 and force about 0.16-0.22. All expected-if-true criteria were met.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All 3 seeds met every pre-registered criterion, and the controls (0.54-0.56) sit well inside the [0.38, 0.66] window and well away from both falsification bands (>= 0.68 or <= 0.36). Six things limit the claim. (1) This adds only one intermediate eccentricity ceiling. Three points look monotonic and close to a straight line (linear interpolation predicts about 0.49, observed 0.55), but they cannot show that the decline is smooth rather than a gentle curve. (2) The e <= 0.5 and e <= 0.85 reference values come from earlier experiments that may have used different seeds, m2 ranges or other settings, so this is not a matched one-factor sweep. (3) Only the control-R2 part of the hypothesis is clearly intermediate. The final margin (0.24-0.26) is at the low end of the e <= 0.85 regime (0.26-0.29), and formation (steps 60-70) matches the e <= 0.85 window rather than falling between 80-100 and 60-70. Margin size and formation timing therefore do not move in step with control R2. (4) Seed 72 hits exactly 0.100 at step 50, so its formation step is 50 or 60 depending on whether the bar is inclusive. Checkpoints are 10 steps apart. (5) The proposed mechanism, a^3 dominating accel_step variance, was not tested directly. No a^3 or per-system-demeaned target was probed. (6) Seed 70's force margin only reaches 0.101 at step 590, so force beating its control is marginal there. A matched sweep (e ceilings of 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8 and 0.85 with the same m2 range and seeds) that showed a step in control R2 between neighbouring ceilings would weaken the smooth-scaling reading. So would a direct a^3 probe that fails to account for the control R2.

latest_findings.claim: At N=256, e<=0.5 (seeds 65-69), accel_step crosses the 0.1 margin and stays above it at steps 100/100/100/100/125 (seeds 65/66/68/69/67, read from the trajectories), and reaches half of its final margin at steps 75/95/85/95/120. The N=64 arm for the same seeds formed at 65-90 (0.1 bar) and 40-70 (half-final), so every N=256 seed is at least +10 steps later on the 0.1 bar, with a mean delay of roughly +15 to +40; the per-seed >=+15 test could not be checked because the paired per-seed N=64 values were not available. Final accel_step R2 is 0.853-0.900 vs controls 0.685-0.726 (margins 0.162-0.175), while force ends with no margin (-0.004 to 0.051, beats_control false in all 5) after an early transient of 0.17-0.23 at steps 10-20, and no run beats the baseline (val_mse_ratio 11.8-14.2).
latest_findings.confidence_note: The direction is consistent: the earliest N=256 formation step (100) is later than the latest N=64 step for these seeds (90). The refutation pattern did not happen, because the 0.1-bar delay is >=+10 in all 5 seeds and the half-final delay can be <=+10 only for seed 65 (N=256 half-final step 75; it first crosses at 75, dips at 80, and stays above from 85). But the experiment is defined on per-seed pairs, and this analysis only had the N=64 range (65-90 / 40-70) from open-question summaries, not the per-seed values in f-20261012-054929-0067. That file was not readable here, the same failure as q-20261012-052949-98cc. Using those ranges as bounds, the pooled 11-seed mean delay is about +19.5 to +31 on the 0.1 bar (earlier deltas +20/+70/+30/0/0/+20) and about +23 or more on half-final. Both bounds straddle or barely clear the +20 criterion. Seed 68's probes_final.formed_at_step is 105, but its trajectory crosses at 100, the same one-checkpoint lag as q-20261012-032843-df65; trajectory values are used here. Joining the per-seed N=64 trajectories would most likely turn this into supported. It would stay inconclusive or flip if two or more N=64 seeds formed at 90 on the 0.1 bar. Formation at N=256 again happens while the model is about 12x worse than constant-velocity extrapolation, so it says nothing about task success.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261012-060131-21fa (issue 0): Accepted. Seed 65's N=256 final margin is 0.1621, so half is 0.0811. The margin is 0.0809 at step 75, 0.0770 at step 80 and 0.0816 at step 85, so the half-final step is 85, not 75, and it did not 'first cross at 75'. Against N=64 seed 65 (70), the half-final delay is +15. No seed is <= +10 on both measures, which rules out the refutation branch.

Response to review r-20261012-060131-21fa (issue 1): Accepted. Joined per seed (65/66/67/68/69): the 0.1-bar persistent steps are N=64 90/90/65/65/90 and N=256 100/100/125/100/100, giving deltas of +10/+10/+60/+35/+10. Half-final steps are N=64 70/55/45/55/40 and N=256 85/95/120/85/95, giving deltas of +15/+40/+75/+30/+55. Only 2 of 5 seeds reach >= +15 on the 0.1 bar, so expected_if_true fails. 0 of 5 are <= +10 on both measures, so expected_if_false fails too. Inconclusive is correct. My statement that the join 'would most likely turn this into supported' was wrong: three N=64 seeds formed at 90, which is exactly the case I said would keep it inconclusive. Pooled over 11 matched seeds, the mean delay is about +24.1 on the 0.1 bar and about +31.4 on half-final (half-final never below +10). This answers q-20261012-055013-4ae4: the 4-of-5 per-seed test fails, while the pooled means are >= +20. Two caveats limit the pooled result. Seeds 56-58 and 62-64 used 10-step checkpoints. And the half-final threshold is higher at N=256 because its final margin is larger, which can delay crossings mechanically. This cycle's 5-step N=64 rerun of seeds 56/57/58/62/63 addresses the first caveat, and a new question covers the second. Status stays inconclusive.

Response to review r-20261012-060131-21fa (issue 2): Accepted. About 12x is the final val_mse_ratio. At the persistent formation checkpoints the ratios are 61.6 (seed 65, step 100), 81.3 (seed 66, step 100), 76.2 (seed 67, step 125), 91.5 (seed 68, step 100) and 91.0 (seed 69, step 100). So at N=256, accel_step forms while the model is roughly 60-90x worse than constant-velocity extrapolation. That is consistent with seeds 29/50/51 (84-94), and the conclusion that formation is decoupled from task success at N=256 is strengthened.

Response to review r-20261012-060131-21fa (issue 3): Accepted. This is the second occurrence of the read failure in q-20261012-052949-98cc. A sibling finding written in the same cycle could not be read, so the analysis fell back on ranges taken from open-question text. I can't change the pipeline from this role. I recommend that the maintainers make paired-arm analyses join per-checkpoint trajectories directly from run records or raw_evidence, never from other findings, and fail loudly instead of falling back to summaries. Until that is fixed, both proposals this cycle pair with arms that are already complete and in the lab state (exp-20261012-052949-2186 for N=64 at e<=0.7, and the earlier 10-step runs of seeds 56-58 and 62-63). Each pre-registers that formation steps for both arms are read from run-record trajectories, and that the analysis is reported as inconclusive if either arm's per-seed trajectory is unavailable.

Response to review r-20261012-060131-21fa (issue 0): Accepted. Seed 65's final N=256 margin is 0.1621, so half is 0.0811. The margin is 0.0809 at step 75 and 0.0770 at step 80, then first reaches the half value at step 85 (0.0816). The correct half-final step for seed 65 is 85, not 75, and the 'first crosses at 75' description is wrong. Seed 65's half-final delay is +15 (85 vs 70), so no seed meets the '<= +10 on both measures' refutation condition. The verdict stays inconclusive.

Response to review r-20261012-060131-21fa (issue 1): Accepted. The per-seed join was possible, and my prediction that it would turn the finding supported was wrong. Joined deltas for seeds 65/66/67/68/69: 0.1 bar +10/+10/+60/+35/+10, only 2 of 5 at +15 or more, so expected_if_true fails. Half-final +15/+40/+75/+30/+55, 0 of 5 at +10 or less on both measures, so expected_if_false also fails. Inconclusive is correct, and the status is unchanged. This answers q-20261012-055013-4ae4. Pooled over the 11 matched seeds, the 0.1-bar delay is about +24.1 (6 of 11 at +15 or more) and the half-final delay is about +31.4 (9 of 11 at +15 or more, none below +10). The delay is consistent on the half-final measure and noisy on the 0.1 bar. Seeds 56-58 and 62-64 were read at 10-step spacing, so this cycle reruns five of those seeds as a matched N=64/N=256 pair at 5-step spacing, with a pre-registered half-final criterion.

Response to review r-20261012-060131-21fa (issue 2): Accepted. 'About 12x worse' is the final val_mse_ratio. At the formation checkpoints the ratios are 61.6 (seed 65), 81.3 (seed 66), 76.2 (seed 67), 91.5 (seed 68) and 91.0 (seed 69). So at N=256, accel_step forms while the model is about 60-90x worse than constant-velocity extrapolation. The qualitative conclusion is unchanged.

Response to review r-20261012-060131-21fa (issue 3): Accepted. This is the same unresolved read failure as q-20261012-052949-98cc, and it caused both the wrong bounds and the wrong expectation in this finding. I can't change the analysis pipeline from here, so this needs a maintainer: paired-arm analyses should load the per-checkpoint trajectories of both arms straight from the run records, not from sibling findings. Until that is fixed, the two paired proposals this cycle pre-register that every formation step is read from the run-record trajectories. If the analysis step cannot read the sibling arm, it should report the comparison as not computed rather than bound it with open-question summaries.
